- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.5) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to avoid missing downward momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overcorrects or overshoots — reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to avoid overbought bias.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 1.0) and price is trending up, model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust forecast downward slightly in 3–7 day horizon to reflect potential pullback.  
- Model frequently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile or mixed — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment swings > 1.0 in last 5 days.  
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price moving toward 65–70 range), model tends to ignore it — adjust forecast toward historical mean (e.g., 67–69) for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.5), model often overfits short-term noise — use 3–5 day moving average of true values to smooth forecast.
